questions.question:

He said, "It's been raining since last night."

options.text: He said that it had rained since last night.
He said that it had been raining since the night before.

questions.solution:

• The structure is: **subject + is/has/have + been + verb (ing) + object.__**
 
• So, the reported speech must be in the past perfect continuous tense.
 
• The structure is: __subject + had + been + verb (ing) + object.__
 
• Example - 
 
 
• ​*He said, "I have been living in Delhi." (Direct)*
 
• *He said that he had been living in Delhi. (Indirect)*
 
 
 
• *​*Therefore, except option 2, no other options are fulfilling the exact rules for Direct-Indirect speech.

• **Since**: In the intervening period between the time mentioned and the time under consideration, typically the present.
 
• "Since" as a preposition is used to introduce a date or a specific time in the past, it is normally used with present perfect and past perfect tenses.
 
• So, according to options "**has been living**" should be used here, which is following the formula of present perfect continuous tense.
 
• **Present perfect continuous:** Something started in the past and is continuing at the present time.
 
• **Structure:** Subject + has/have + been + verb (ing) + Object__

Therefore, the correct answer is **option 1**, which can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

**Corrected sentence:** *Manoj __has been living__ in the city since 1993.*

questions.question: When the government resorts to borrowing only to clear the backlog of interest payments, it is referred to as __________.
questions.solution:

__
 
• **Zero primary deficit**

 
 
• **​Zero primary deficit means the government resorts to borrowing only to clear the existing backlog of interest payments.**
 
• It is not adding to the existing loans for any purpose other than meeting its existing obligations of interest payment.
 
• It is a sign of fiscal discipline or fiscal responsibility on the part of the government.
 
• A high primary deficit, on the other hand, reflects the fiscal irresponsibility of the government.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Zero revenue deficit **

 
 
• **The shortfall of total revenue receipts compared to total revenue expenditure is defined as a revenue deficit.**
 
• It is related to only revenue expenditure and revenue receipts of the government.
 
• It signifies that the government’s own earnings are insufficient to meet the normal functioning of government departments.
 
• Revenue deficit** results in borrowing.**
 
 
 
• **Zero fiscal deficit**
 
 
• **A fiscal deficit is estimated as the difference between total expenditure and total receipts.**
 
• The Gross fiscal deficit is also estimated as the sum total of borrowing from RBI.
 
• **​**The fiscal deficit in the economy will be zero if there is no provision for borrowings in the budget.
 
 
 
• **Excess budget deficit**
 
 
• **A budget deficit occurs when expenses exceed revenue.**
 
• The government generally uses the term budget deficit when referring to spending rather than businesses or individuals. 
 
• Countries can counter budget deficits by raising taxes and cutting spending.
